name: Some Poster
tagline: AI tool for turning ideas into social posts and publishing them on a schedule.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The generation half of this is a prompt template and a text box, and an agent will nail it in an afternoon. The publishing half is where every DIY social tool dies: each platform wants its own OAuth app, review process, rate limits, and media upload dance, and those change often enough to become a chore you did not sign up for. If you are willing to live with a local drafts queue that you copy-paste into each app yourself, the personal version is genuinely fine and probably better tuned to your voice. If you want scheduled auto-publishing to several networks with previews that match the real thing, you are buying maintenance, not code. Build it, then decide how much you hate pasting.
coreLoopDIY: A local app that takes a topic or a URL, drafts platform-sized posts in your voice with an LLM, stores them in a scheduled queue, and reminds you to post or pushes to the one or two networks you bothered to wire up.
requirements: Optional: a developer app plus tokens for any network you want to auto-publish to
Somewhere always-on if you want scheduling to fire while you sleep
whatYouLose: Multi-network publishing that already works: no OAuth apps to register, no API review, no token refresh code to babysit
Accurate per-platform previews and character/media rules that someone else keeps current
Mobile access, so scheduling and approving from a phone is on you
Analytics on what actually performed, which is most of why people schedule at all
Team review flows, shared calendars, and the audit trail that comes with them
moatNotes: The moat is not the model, it is the boring maintenance of half a dozen platform APIs that keep moving.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because nobody wants to be the on-call engineer for someone else's API deprecation notice. Paying converts a recurring maintenance liability into a line item, and it buys the parts that are annoying rather than hard: real previews, media handling, retries when a post fails at 6am, and a phone app for the moment you spot a typo. If posting is part of your job, that trade is easy. If you post twice a week for yourself, a local drafter and a calendar reminder covers it.
notes: Cheap to build, expensive to keep working, which is the usual shape of anything that touches social platform APIs.
prompt:
Build a local-first social post drafter and scheduler called "Deskposter". No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable: Node 20, TypeScript, Next.js App Router, SQLite via better-sqlite3, Tailwind for styling. Everything runs with `npm run dev` on localhost. Single user, no auth.

Core loop:
1. Input box accepts a raw idea, a pasted article, or a URL (fetch and extract readable text with @mozilla/readability + jsdom).
2. Call an OpenAI-compatible chat API using OPENAI_API_KEY and OPENAI_BASE_URL from .env to draft posts for the selected targets: x (280 chars), linkedin (long form), mastodon (500 chars), threads. Generate 3 variants per target in one request, streaming to the UI.
3. A persistent "voice profile" stored in SQLite: tone notes plus up to 20 example posts I paste in. Inject it into every prompt.
4. Editable draft view with live character counting and a hard warning past each platform limit.
5. Save drafts to a queue with a scheduled datetime and status (draft | scheduled | posted | skipped).

Scheduling: an in-process node-cron job checks every minute. If a due post has an outbound adapter configured, publish it; otherwise mark it "due" and surface it in a Due Now panel with a one-click copy button per platform. Log every attempt with the response or error.

Adapters: implement exactly two, behind a shared interface, both optional and skipped when env vars are missing: Mastodon (access token, simple POST to /api/v1/statuses) and a generic webhook POST. Do not attempt X or LinkedIn OAuth. Leave a documented stub file explaining where to add them.

Also include: a week calendar view of the queue, CSV export of all posts, and a /health route.

Out of scope, do not build: analytics, image generation, team roles, multi-workspace, payment, a mobile app, or hosted deployment config.

Secrets only in .env, ship .env.example. Write a README with setup in under 10 lines and a blunt note that auto-publishing works for Mastodon and webhooks only.
